texts_above.2: SP lost several seconds before checking the indications, because of a brief hesitation over whether to look inside while the position was degrading, but then confirmed normal engine operation and continued as a separate takeoff without prompting. Crosschecking the indications immediately the aircraft begins to fall behind, rather than hesitating first, would close that margin further. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to competent crosscheck discipline when falling behind.
texts_above.3: SP recognized that the aircraft was falling behind, crosschecked the engine instruments and the airspeed indicator without delay and, having confirmed no problem, continued as a separate takeoff, with aircraft control and runway alignment maintained throughout the crosscheck. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to well-developed crosscheck discipline when falling behind.
texts_above.4: SP detected the aft drift at its onset, crosschecked the engine instruments and the airspeed indicator in a single deliberate scan and reached the continue or abort decision with ample runway remaining, without interrupting the outside picture on Number 1. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to outstanding crosscheck discipline when falling behind.

error_modes.label: Sympathetic abort after brake release
error_modes.source: technique:9.42 FORMATION TAKEOFF ABNORMALITIES AND ABORTS

texts.0: SP, due to reacting to Number 1's abort call by retarding the PCL after brake release, executed a sympathetic abort that is not called for once the roll has started and added a second aircraft to a high speed abort situation. The aircraft was also allowed to drift off its respective side of the runway during the deceleration, reducing the separation from the aborting aircraft. IP took control, restored the aircraft to its own side of the runway and managed the stop.
texts.1: SP, due to hesitation over whether Number 1's abort applied to him, brought the PCL back after brake release before deciding to continue the takeoff. The power reduction was reversed only after the IP directed MAX power, by which time the aircraft had decelerated to the limit of what allowed a normal continuation. The respective side of the runway was maintained but the radio call was omitted until prompted.
texts.2: SP, due to a momentary startle at Number 1's abort call, moved the PCL back briefly after brake release instead of continuing the single ship takeoff. SP recognized within a second or two that no sympathetic abort was required, advanced the PCL to MAX, held his respective side of the runway and completed a normal takeoff. The radio call was made as soon as practical, without any intervention.
texts.3: SP continued the takeoff when Number 1 aborted after brake release, advancing the PCL to MAX power, maintaining his own side of the runway and executing a normal single ship takeoff. Runway alignment was held within the tolerance throughout and a radio call was made as soon as practical. Aircraft control was not sacrificed to make the transmission.
texts.4: SP responded to Number 1's abort without any sympathetic power reduction, advancing to MAX power immediately and flying an accurate single ship takeoff on his own side of the runway. Separation from the aborting aircraft was preserved at every stage and the radio call was made only once the aircraft was safely established. The whole sequence was handled with no disturbance to the flight path.
texts.marginal: SP continued the takeoff and kept to his own side of the runway within standards, but the initial reaction to the abort call included a perceptible PCL movement before the decision to continue was made. The trend shows the abort call being answered reflexively rather than assessed against the point in the roll. SP is expected to confirm that no sympathetic abort is required and to hold the power setting steady while doing so.

texts_at.1: SP reversed the power reduction only after IP directed MAX power, having decelerated to the limit of what allowed a normal continuation while hesitating over whether Number 1's abort applied. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to confirm no sympathetic abort is required and hold takeoff power without needing MAX power directed.
texts_at.2: SP moved the PCL back briefly after brake release because of a momentary startle at Number 1's abort call, then recognized within a second or two that no sympathetic abort was required and advanced the PCL to MAX without prompting. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to check the own aircraft state before any PCL movement rather than reacting to the call first.
texts_at.3: SP continued the takeoff without a sympathetic power reduction on three of the four occasions when a call was heard nearby, the fourth showing a brief PCL movement before the decision to continue was made. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to hold takeoff power on that one occasion as steadily as the first three.

texts_above.2: SP moved the PCL back briefly after brake release because of a momentary startle at Number 1's abort call, but recognized within a second or two that no sympathetic abort was required and advanced the PCL to MAX without prompting, completing a normal takeoff. Checking the own aircraft state before any PCL movement, rather than reacting to the call first, would close that margin further. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to steady power discipline on a sympathetic abort.
texts_above.3: SP continued the takeoff when Number 1 aborted after brake release, advancing the PCL to MAX power, maintaining the own side of the runway and executing a normal single ship takeoff with aircraft control never sacrificed to make the radio call. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to well-developed power discipline on a sympathetic abort.
texts_above.4: SP responded to Number 1's abort without any sympathetic power reduction, advancing to MAX power immediately and flying an accurate single ship takeoff with separation from the aborting aircraft preserved at every stage. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to outstanding power discipline on a sympathetic abort.
